No, there is no definitive meaning to life, which is not to say that it isn't valuable to the living. We are animals, shaped by directionless and indifferent forces. Our lives merely have subjective meaning, which differs from person to person and can change on a whim depending on the circumstances.
I'm pretty sure the "meaning of life" is to reproduce, since it's one common trait among all living beings.

I would argue that love is too slim an answer. The meaning of life has to do with human connection, and love is a big part of that, but it's not everything.

Sure, on a level of personal fulfillment, experiencing all the different kinds of romantic, familial, fraternal, and platonic love can really broaden your worldview and make you feel good, but there's so much more to life than the personal.

Just look at industry, art, or even sports. There are plenty of ways humans connect with one another to accomplish things much greater than any one person. And yet, in each accomplishment, every person plays an integral role. This feeling of transcendence of the self can be experienced in a group as mundane as your high school marching band.

Human connection can also be experienced through art. Take Whitman's classic poem "Crossing Brooklyn Ferry," where he explicitly addresses the reader in a way that feels very personal. Even though he is dead, the reader sees a glimpse of Whitman's soul through his work, and in that way he transcends his death. More recently, David Bowie's album Blackstar, which he released right before his death, is a work of art so strong that I would say he transcended death in its writing. He touches on universal themes by giving a window into his individual, personal life experience, which creates truth, insight, and beauty.

So I guess what I'm saying is: love is part of the meaning of life. To understand the meaning of life you must transcend it, and then transcend your death through the mark you leave on the world and it's people. Love can take you out of your body, just like working in a group, making art, making something useful, organizing a community, or even taking psychedelic drugs. But none of these things by themselves are the meaning of life--they only grasp at it.

Do everything, meet everyone, go everywhere.

Learn everything, influence everyone, become immortal.

Or at least that's the goal.
